newsitem.title: USA: Web commerce seen reaching $220 bln in 2001 - IDC.
newsitem.headline: Web commerce seen reaching $220 bln in 2001 - IDC.

text.p: Commerce on the World Wide Web is expected to grow from $2.6 billion last year to more than $220 billion in 2001, according to a report by International Data Corporation (IDC).
The worldwide growth will be spurred by the increasing number of Web users and the average transaction size.
"Based on IDC's Internet Commerce Market Model, IDC forecasts untrammeled growth in Internet and World Wide Web use around the world," said John Gantz, IDC senior vice president.

IDC, owned by the International Data Group media and research company, said the report is based on more than 40,000 primary research interviews per year in 17 countries and on IDC's vaunted supply-side forecasts for personal computers, network computers, modems, and other technologies.

The report said the number of devices accessing the Web will grow from 32 million last year to more than 300 million by the end of 2001. The number of users associated with the devices will grow from 28 million to 175 million in the same time period.
